Equal intensity k-means space partitioning (EI-kMeans)

Source: R/dfr_eikmeans.R
eikmeans.Rd

Histogram-based two-sample test for drift detection (Liu et al., 2021). The feature space is partitioned by k-means clusters of (nearly) equal intensity, so that no bin straddles a gap between clusters of the data, and a new sample is compared with the training sample by Pearson's chi-square test on the counts of the two samples in every bin.

Usage

eikmeans(
  training,
  n_test,
  k = 40,
  alpha = 0.05,
  min_points = 50,
  n_build = 2000,
  thetas = seq(0, 0.95, by = 0.05)
)

Arguments

training

The training sample (matrix or data frame of numeric features).

n_test

Size of the samples that will be tested. The number of bins is at most n_test / 5, so that the expected count of every bin in a test sample is at least 5.

k

Largest number of bins.

alpha

Significance level of the chi-square test.

min_points

Smallest number of training points per bin (beta).

n_build

Number of training points used to build the partitioning: the first n_build rows. The counts of the bins are then taken from the whole training sample.

thetas

Values of the shape parameter theta of the amplify-shrink coefficients exp(theta (r - 1)), tried in order.

Value

An eikmeans object with the centroids (centers), the amplify-shrink coefficients (amplify), the training counts of every bin (counts) and the settings.

Details

The partitioning follows the reference code (https://github.com/Anjin-Liu/TCYB2019-EIkMeansDriftDetection):

  1. The number of bins starts at min(k, n_test / 5, n / 50) (n is the training size).

  2. Greedy equal intensity initialization (Algorithm 1): K - 1 times, the point whose n_build / K-th nearest neighbour is farthest is taken together with its n_build / K nearest neighbours as a group, and the group is removed; the remaining points are the last group. The first point of every group starts k-means (Lloyd's algorithm, with the stopping rule of scikit-learn).

  3. Amplify-shrink (Algorithm 2): with intensity ratios r (points per cluster over n_build / K), a point goes to the cluster that minimises its distance times exp(theta (r - 1)), so crowded clusters shrink and sparse ones grow. The ratios are updated after every theta, and the search stops when every cluster has more than min_points points. If no theta is enough, the number of bins is lowered by one and the search repeated.

  4. A test sample is assigned to the bins in the same way, and the 2 x K table of training and test counts is tested with Pearson's chi-square test (Algorithm 3); bins empty in both samples are left out, and the Yates correction is used with one degree of freedom, as in scipy.stats.chi2_contingency.

The reference code differs from the paper in a few points, and the code is followed: theta ranges over 0, 0.05, ..., 0.95 (the paper gives up to 1.5), the initialization uses the distance to the n / K-th neighbour (the paper describes the nearest one) and starts k-means from a point of each group (the paper, from the group mean), the starting number of bins depends on the test size, and the partitioning is built on the first 2000 training points. If the number of bins reaches 1, the reference falls back to k plain k-means clusters; so does this implementation.

References

Liu, A., Lu, J. and Zhang, G. (2021). Concept drift detection via equal intensity k-means space partitioning. IEEE Transactions on Cybernetics, 51(6), 3198-3211. doi:10.1109/TCYB.2020.2983962

See also

eikmeans_test() to test a sample and dfr_eikmeans() to monitor a stream.

Examples

# Two clusters; the right one moves.
set.seed(1)
cluster <- function(n, x) cbind(stats::rnorm(n, x), stats::rnorm(n))
training <- rbind(cluster(1000, 0), cluster(1000, 5))
model <- eikmeans(training, n_test = 200)
nrow(model$centers)
#> [1] 22
eikmeans_test(model, rbind(cluster(100, 0), cluster(100, 5)))
#>   statistic df   p_value drift
#> 1  16.25849 21 0.7549563 FALSE
eikmeans_test(model, rbind(cluster(100, 0), cluster(100, 5.8)))
#>   statistic df      p_value drift
#> 1  75.42494 21 4.626624e-08  TRUE
